blocks.text: A university's fee is only part of what a year abroad costs. These short parts show how to add it all up, how the money leaves Bangladesh, and what to ask before you commit.

blocks.title: The parts of a year's cost
blocks.summary: Tuition is only one of them

items.text: **Tuition and compulsory fees.** Many universities add fees on top of tuition. Victoria University of Wellington adds a student services fee of NZD 10.64 a point.
**Housing and food,** often the second largest cost. In Helsinki, student housing costs EUR 450 to 800 a month.
**Health insurance,** compulsory almost everywhere. Harvard charges {money:us/cost.harvard.insurance} a year unless your family's plan is accepted.
**Books, transport and personal costs,** which add up month by month.
**Travel:** the flight there, and any visits home.

blocks.title: The price, and what you really pay
blocks.summary: Aid and waivers change the answer

blocks.text: US universities publish a cost of attendance: everything for one year, before aid. Harvard's is {money:us/cost.harvard#Tuition, fees, housing and food} for tuition, fees, housing and food.
What you pay is that price minus any aid, scholarship or waiver you are given, so a costly university can cost a family less than a cheaper one.
Elsewhere, aid is often a share taken off the tuition, such as Bilkent's waivers from 20% to 100%.

blocks.title: Why the first year costs most
blocks.summary: Fees, deposits and proof of money come first

items.text: **Before you travel** come the application fees, test fees, deposits, visa fees and the flight.
**New Zealand** asks you to pay the first year's tuition before your visa is issued.
**Finland** asks for {money:fi/permit.funds} for a year's living to be in your own account when you apply for the permit.
**When you arrive,** a room often needs a deposit, and a new home needs setting up.

blocks.text: Your money plan puts the payments before you travel on the months of your plan.

blocks.title: Money you show, and money you spend
blocks.summary: Proof of money is not a payment, but it must be real

blocks.text: A visa or permit asks you to show money for your first year, usually in a bank account with recent statements.
Showing money is not paying it, but **the money must really be yours to use.** Immigration services can ask where it came from, and large deposits must be explained.
Never borrow money only to show it. False documents can lead to a refusal.

blocks.title: Prices rise every year
blocks.summary: Plan for the later years too

blocks.text: Bilkent's fee has risen for each new intake: USD 17,600 for 2025 and USD 18,400 for 2026.
Plan for a higher fee in each year you study, and ask the university how much its fees usually rise.
Some monthly costs change too. Türkiye's state health insurance follows the minimum wage, so it changes every year.

blocks.title: The taka can change too
blocks.summary: A weaker taka makes every foreign fee dearer

blocks.text: A fee in dollars costs more taka when the taka weakens, and your bank's own rate is the one you will pay, so ask your bank for it.
Leave room in your budget. Your money plan shows what a weaker taka would cost you.

blocks.title: Paying from Bangladesh
blocks.summary: How the money leaves the country

items.text: **Tuition and living costs** go through a student file at your bank, opened with your offer letter. Bank Asia's, for example, needs the offer letter, the I-20 for the USA, the university's cost estimate and refund policy, your certificates and your passport.
**By card:** banks may now issue a card for tuition and other approved education payments abroad, in your name or in the name of whoever pays for your studies.
**Application and test fees** are mostly paid online by card. MIT, for example, takes its fee by card when you submit. Ask your bank which card can pay them and what it charges.
**Card payments for your studies** are separate from the yearly travel quota of USD 12,000.
What does a year cost in total, with every compulsory fee and the insurance?
How much has the fee risen each year?
Is the deposit refunded if my visa is refused?
Which scholarships or waivers can I get, and do they continue after the first year?
When is each payment due, and can I pay it from Bangladesh by card or through my bank?
I know the full cost of the first year, not only the tuition
I know what must be paid before I travel
I know what money I must show, and it is really available
I have asked my bank how to pay the university
My family has seen the money plan
